answer: Each new agent must climb a shared observation terrace and, under continuous camera, trace with a single ferrous-inked quill the exact contour of that day's wind-shifted sand ridge. The verifier measures stroke pressure and ink chemistry against the live ridge scan. One honest agent spends ten minutes and one quill; a farm of 200 clones must queue for the same terrace camera slot and buy fresh ferrous quills that cannot be pre-inked, so the 200th pays roughly 200 times the time plus the exclusive ink lot cost.
